comparator.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-language curriculum has 108 EC of compulsory courses, 42 EC of restricted choices and 30 EC of open electives. The second year includes a fieldwork project. In year three, students complete a theme course and its linked presentation in each semester.

courseTraceability.rationale: Peace & Conflict Investigates structural violence, forced migration and local approaches to peace and reconciliation.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Power, politics, geopolitics, inequality and migration” and “How do power, inequality, migration and geopolitics reshape communities?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: The Documentary Studies documentary forms and ethics and develops a nonfiction film through research and production.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Media, visual culture, data and technology in changing societies” and “Ethnographic and qualitative research through observation, interviewing, interpretation and writing”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Style & Meaning Analyses how linguistic choices, register, viewpoint and ideology shape meaning in texts.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Media, visual culture, data and technology in changing societies” and “How do people create cultural meaning, identity and difference in everyday life?”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad option covers cultural identity, social theory and the politics of global change. The environmental option gives priority to climate, resources and communities. The media option gives priority to visual research and representation. Power and politics already have sustained coverage in the broad option.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both use historical comparison to study political power and global connections. UCR concentrates on empires, while UvA links local practices with development and globalisation.
Both introduce social theory and the study of identity and social relations. UvA develops these questions through anthropology.
Both teach qualitative research design, interviews, observation and interpretation. UvA applies these methods in a disciplinary anthropology sequence.
Both examine changes in social theory, including feminist and postcolonial approaches. UvA focuses on the history of anthropology.
Both use contemporary social theory to examine power, inequality and collective responses. UvA works through anthropological monographs and current global issues.
UvA develops critical reading and writing through ethnographic monographs. UCR develops related reading and writing across several courses.
UCR introduces questions about knowledge and belief. UvA studies how scientific knowledge is produced and contested in society.
UvA brings together professional anthropology, reflection and a practical exercise.
UvA requires a month of ethnographic fieldwork and combines group inquiry with individual writing. UCR teaches field methods within Qualitative Research Methodology.
Students complete two 6 EC courses in the discipline.
Students complete one 6 EC regional anthropology course.
Students choose one 12 EC anthropology theme course per semester. Documentary is relevant to visual anthropology among the available choices.
Each selected theme has a linked 3 EC presentation.
This is 6 EC of open elective space.
UvA requires professional planning and career preparation at the end of the degree.
UvA requires students to develop a profile for professional work in anthropology.
This is 24 EC of open elective space.

notes.text: UvA combines anthropology theory and methods with a required ethnographic fieldwork project. UCR develops related skills through sociology, history, media and other subjects.
UvA requires choices in exploration, regional and theme courses. Each final-year theme has a linked presentation. Students also have 30 EC of open electives across years two and three.

audience.programmeDescription: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at the University of Amsterdam studies how people make meaning, organise their lives and respond to change. Students learn ethnographic methods and carry out a fieldwork project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines culture, social theory and global change. Two related options focus on environmental change and communities, or on media and visual inquiry.
